# MDL112 · `bracket-leak-risk`

<!-- Generated by tools/gendocs from internal/rules: do not edit. -->

An empty line placed after this line would make mydumper ignore the file.

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | loading |
| Default severity | warning |
| Fix | — |
| Flags | unsuppressible |
| Design references | P1, case 58 |

## Why

After a line that contains `[` after other text (a comment such as `# see [docs]`, an indented `  [mydumper]`, a localized key `key[fr]=v`), mydumper's pre-processor does not reset its state (see MDL108). The file loads today because no empty line follows, but adding one, by hand or by a script that appends a block starting with an empty line, makes GLib reject the file.

It is a warning when the line is the last one of the file (a script appending to the file is the typical way this breaks), information otherwise. Remove the `[` from the comment, or de-indent the header.

## Example

❌ Before:

```ini
[mydumper]
threads=4
# see [docs]
```

```text
3:1-3:13 warning MDL112[bracket-leak-risk] line contains `[` after other text: an empty line placed right after line 3 would make mydumper's pre-processor produce `= 1`, which GLib rejects
  = If a block starting with an empty line is appended to this file (for example "\n[client]" added by a script), mydumper will ignore the entire file.
```

## Configuration

Enabled by default. To change its severity or turn it off:

```yaml
rules:
  severity:
    MDL112: warning   # or error, info, off
```

Its diagnostics mean mydumper ignores the whole file: they cannot be suppressed by comments, only by the configuration or `--ignore`.
